page: Amazon Web Services c8gb.48xlarge is a high-density, compute-optimized instance built on AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processors managed by the AWS Nitro System. It provides 192 dedicated physical CPU cores operating at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz, using a one-thread-per-core configuration without simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is set at 384 GB, providing a standard compute-optimized ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Cache infrastructure includes 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 36 MB L3 cache. The instance features a 400 Gbps baseline network interface. No local disk storage is included, requiring users to rely on external network-attached volumes for data persistence.

Benchmark measurements reflect the multi-threaded capabilities of its 192-core architecture. In multi-core CPU evaluations, the instance achieves top-tier results, including a score of 314,716.71 in stress-ng multi-core tests and strong results in PassMark CPU (77,457.05) and Geekbench multi-core (20,128.0). It demonstrates exceptional throughput in software compilation via Clang (87,780.0) and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (1,427.22 GB/sec). Memory subsystem throughput is equally prominent, recording 959.17 GB/sec in large-block uncached reads and 21,328.86 GB/sec in cached reads. Network and service benchmarking confirms high capacity, yielding 355.94 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations and 219.73 GB/sec in static web serving tests. Conversely, single-core benchmarks, such as single-threaded gzip compression (29.06 GB/sec) and Geekbench single-core (1,652.0), fall into middle-tier bands.

The architectural profile presents clear operational tradeoffs. With dedicated single-threaded cores, execution avoids resource contention, ensuring consistent execution times under heavy parallel loads. However, applications dependent on strict single-thread latency will find average performance levels rather than class-leading speeds. Furthermore, the absence of integrated NVMe storage requires all persistent I/O to traverse the network, though the 400 Gbps interface provides substantial headroom. The high density of physical ARM cores offers favorable compute efficiency for massively distributed tasks. AWS c8gb.48xlarge is well aligned for scalable parallel workloads, including distributed continuous integration and compilation pipelines, in-memory caching layers, high-volume web serving, and compute-bound simulation clusters.
description: Amazon Web Services c8gb.48xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and custom AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processors. The configuration features 192 dedicated physical cores clocked at 2.7 GHz with a single thread per core, paired with 384 GB of memory to maintain a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio. Network capacity is provisioned at a 400 Gbps baseline, while internal persistent local storage is absent. Across synthetic and real-world benchmarks, the instance demonstrates top-tier multi-threaded throughput, achieving 314,716.71 in stress-ng multi-core testing, 355.94 million operations per second in Redis SET tests, and 219.73 GB/s in static web serving throughput. Single-core performance falls in the average category, highlighting an architecture geared towards massive concurrency rather than single-threaded execution speed. The server delivers high resource density for parallel tasks, making it suited for large-scale code compilation, high-throughput distributed database operations, static web serving, and batch compute workloads.
